properties.description: Nickel hydroxide on nickel sulfide/nickel foam composite

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.25 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 4 mmol NH4F and 10 mmol urea were dissolved in 35 mL DIW. It was then poured into a 45 mL autoclave and put in two pieces of NF (1×3 cm²). The autoclave was placed in an oven and heated at 120°C for 6 h. Finally, the Ni(OH)2/NF was washed with DIW and dried in a vacuum oven.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni(OH)2/NF: 2.25 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 4 mmol NH4F and 10 mmol urea were dissolved in 35 mL DIW... heated at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfuration
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni(OH)2/NF was put in a solution consisting of 25 mL ethanol and 2.5 mL 2-mercaptoethanol. Then it was placed in 45 mL autoclave and heated at 150°C for 5 h. The obtained Ni3S2/NF was finally washed several times in DIW and alcohol and dried in a vacuum oven.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni3S2/NF: A piece of Ni(OH)2/NF was put in a solution consisting of 25 mL ethanol and 2.5 mL 2-mercaptoethanol... heated at 150°C for 5 h.

nodes.name: Electrochemical activation
nodes.procedure: The Ni3S2/NF (1×1 cm²) was in situ electrochemically activated for 12 h at a voltage of -1.5 V (vs Hg/HgO) via a standard three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH. Then the sample was washed in DIW and vacuum dried to obtain Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF: The Ni3S2/NF (1×1 cm²) was in situ electrochemically activated for 12 h at a voltage of -1.5 V (vs Hg/HgO)...

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: The fabrication process of NiFe LDH/NF was similar to that of Ni(OH)2/NF except that 0.25 mmol Fe(NO3)2·9H2O was added and the amount of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O was 2 mmol. [Expanded from Ni(OH)2/NF procedure: 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.25 mmol Fe(NO3)2·9H2O, 4 mmol NH4F and 10 mmol urea were dissolved in 35 mL DIW. It was then poured into a 45 mL autoclave and put in NF (1×3 cm²). The autoclave was placed in an oven and heated at 120°C for 6 h. Finally, the NiFe LDH/NF was washed with DIW and dried in a vacuum oven.]
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiFe LDH/NF: The fabrication process of NiFe LDH/NF was similar to that of Ni(OH)2/NF except that 0.25 mmol Fe(NO3)2·9H2O was added and the amount of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O was 2 mmol.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF is consistent with Ni3S2/NF, showing diffraction peaks at 2θ = 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.4° for NF substrate and other peaks corresponding to Ni3S2 with no other crystalline phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF is consistent with that of Ni3S2/NF (Figure S2a, Supporting Information), as shown in Figure 1a.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF maintains nanosheet morphology composed of particles similar to Ni3S2/NF but with significantly increased nanosheet thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF (Figure 1b-c) sample clearly shows that the nanosheets composed of particles morphology remains consistent with Ni3S2/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF nanosheet morphology composed of particles with amorphous layer and micropores of average diameter 1.65 nm in nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1d, the TEM image further revealed that Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF is the morphology of nanosheets composed of particles as well as an amorphous layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows outer surface without lattice fringes and inner region with 0.29 nm lattice fringes corresponding to (110) plane of Ni3S2, confirming amorphous Ni(OH)x on Ni3S2 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1e), unlike the outer surface (region I) without obvious lattice fringes, the inner (region II) observed lattice fringes of 0.29 nm corresponding to the (110) lattice plane of Ni3S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, S, and O elements throughout Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF with significantly increased O molarity compared to Ni3S2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of element mapping (Figure 1f-i) show that Ni, S, and O elements are uniform distribution throughout Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF was subsequently subjected to energy dispersive spectrometry (EDS) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES spectra show the near-edge energy of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 positioned between Ni3S2 and Ni(OH)2, confirming higher Ni valence state than Ni3S2 but lower than Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of samples (Figure 2a) displays that the near-edge energy of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 is between Ni3S2 and Ni(OH)2 which confirms that the valence state of Ni elements in Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 is higher than that of in Ni3S2 and lower than that of in Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT EXAFS of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 shows Ni-S at 1.91 Å, Ni-O at 1.56 Å, Ni-Ni at 2.69 Å; WT shows Ni-S scattering max at ≈5.9 Å⁻¹ and Ni-O at ≈7.9 Å⁻¹ confirming heterostructure formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transforms (FT) of Ni K-edge spectra for Ni3S2 exhibit a main peak at a radial distance of 1.83Å corresponding to the Ni-S bond. Compared with pristine Ni3S2 except for the peak contributed by the Ni-S bond (1.91 Å), the peaks at 1.56 and 2.69Å belonged to Ni-O and Ni-Ni bond are also shown in the spectra of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Ni 2p of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 shows Ni(OH)x peaks at 875.25 eV (2p1/2) and 856.80 eV (2p3/2); Ni3S2 peaks positively shifted to 872.92 eV and 855.18 eV (Δ≈0.4 eV); S 2p negatively shifted indicating electron transfer from Ni to S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2, two peaks belonging to Ni(OH)x appear at 875.25 and 856.80 eV. Interestingly, the peaks of Ni 2p1/2 (872.92 eV) and Ni 2p3/2 (855.18 eV) of Ni3S2 exhibit a positive shift of ≈0.37 and ≈0.43 eV... the peaks of S 2p1/2 (163.36 eV) and S 2p3/2 (162.29 eV) in Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 exhibit a negative shift of ≈0.26 and ≈0.22 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR detects -OH species in Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 sample confirming amorphous Ni(OH)x presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) detected the appearance of '-OH' species in Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 sample, further confirming the existence of amorphous Ni(OH)x.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle measurement shows Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF is super-hydrophilic with 0° angle vs 146° for hydrophobic Ni3S2/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2g-h and Figure S6, Supporting Information, the contact angle of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2 is 0°, which is significantly smaller than that of Ni3S2 (146°).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates (5-150 mV/s) used to determine Cdl = 113.2 mF/cm² for Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF (vs 21.4 mF/cm² for Ni3S2/NF), indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of catalysts is usually evaluated by the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) obtained via CV method (Figure S7, Supporting Information) ... the Cdl of Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF (113.2 mF cm⁻²) was larger than that of Ni3S2/NF (21.4 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.6 Ω for Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF vs 4.2 Ω for Ni3S2/NF, indicating faster HER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) in Figure 3g shows that Ni(OH)x/Ni3S2/NF (0.6 Ω) has a lower charge transfer resistance (Rct) than Ni3S2/NF (4.2 Ω).
